## Description

Add a `partio checkpoint delete <checkpoint-id>` command that removes a specific checkpoint from the orphan branch by ID. This complements the existing `partio prune` command (which removes checkpoints by age) with targeted, individual deletion. Inspired by [entireio/cli changelog v0.7.7](https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.7.7), which added an `entire trail delete` subcommand.

## What to build

Add a `checkpoint` subcommand group to the CLI with an initial `delete` subcommand:

- `partio checkpoint delete <checkpoint-id>` removes the named checkpoint from the `partio/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch by rewriting its tree without that entry.
- Add a `Delete(id string) error` method to `*Store` in `internal/checkpoint/` (alongside the existing `Prune` method) that:
  1. Locates the checkpoint in the orphan branch by its shard (`id[:2]`) and rest (`id[2:]`).
  2. Returns a clear error when the checkpoint does not exist.
  3. Rebuilds the root tree and shard tree without the deleted entry (reuse the `rebuildTreeWithout` pattern from `prune.go`).
  4. Creates a new commit on the orphan branch referencing the rebuilt tree.
  5. Advances `refs/heads/partio/checkpoints/v1` to the new commit.
- The CLI command confirms before deleting unless `--force` is passed.
- Register the `checkpoint` parent command in `cmd/partio/main.go`'s `newRootCmd()`.

**Note (argos review, 2026-10-10).** Like `partio prune`, this makes a new commit whose parent is the old tip (`internal/checkpoint/prune.go:110`). So the deleted checkpoint stays in the history of the checkpoint branch, and on the remote after a push. Say this in the command help and in its output, so that nobody uses the command to remove a leaked secret: that needs a history rewrite and a force push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `partio checkpoint delete <id>` removes the named checkpoint from the orphan branch
- [ ] Deleting a checkpoint that does not exist returns a non-zero exit code and a clear error message
- [ ] Running without `--force` prompts for confirmation; `--force` skips the prompt
- [ ] After deletion the orphan branch no longer contains the deleted checkpoint's tree entry
- [ ] The command is registered under a new `checkpoint` parent command in `newRootCmd()`
- [ ] The help text and the output say that the checkpoint stays in the branch history and on the remote

## Premise

<!-- partio:premise:v1 -->

- `partio prune` exists and removes checkpoints only by age, not by individual ID [evidence: `cmd/partio/prune.go`]
- No individual-checkpoint delete command exists in the CLI [evidence: `cmd/partio/`]
- Checkpoints are stored on `partio/checkpoints/v1` as a two-level shard tree, readable by `checkpoint.Read(id string)` [evidence: `internal/checkpoint/read.go`]

## Gathered Evidence

**Claim 1:** `partio prune` exists and removes checkpoints only by age, not by individual ID
Evidence: `cmd/partio/prune.go` and `internal/checkpoint/prune.go`
Verdict: holds
Excerpt: `cmd/partio/prune.go:30: cmd.Flags().StringVar(&olderThan, "older-than", "90d", ...)` and `internal/checkpoint/prune.go: func (s *Store) Prune(olderThan time.Duration, currentCommitHash string, dryRun bool)`. The only deletion parameter is a time duration; no ID-based path exists.

**Claim 2:** No individual-checkpoint delete command exists in the CLI
Evidence: `cmd/partio/` directory listing
Verdict: holds
Excerpt: Files in `cmd/partio/`: clean.go, cleanup_sessions.go, disable.go, doctor.go, enable.go, explain.go, hook.go, main.go, prune.go, reset.go, resume.go, rewind.go, status.go, version.go. No file implementing a checkpoint-by-ID delete command. `main.go` registers: version, enable, disable, status, hook, doctor, reset, clean, rewind, resume, prune, cleanup, explain — no checkpoint delete.

**Claim 3:** Checkpoints are stored on `partio/checkpoints/v1` as a two-level shard tree, readable by `checkpoint.Read(id string)`
Evidence: `internal/checkpoint/read.go`, `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`
Verdict: holds
Excerpt: `read.go: func Read(id string) (*CheckpointData, error)` uses `Shard(id)` and `Rest(id)` to locate `partio/checkpoints/v1:<shard>/<rest>/metadata.json`. `checkpoint.go: func Shard(id string) string { return id[:2] }`.
